help.intro: A text of about 200 words about German beer and the oldest food law still in force: in 1516 two Bavarian dukes ordered that beer may be brewed only from water, barley and hops, and the rule still shapes what is in a German glass today. The text tells how beer is brewed, how many breweries there are, why the Oktoberfest started as a wedding, and how much is drunk there. All facts are real and were checked. You read what you have just learnt: the passive in the present (Das Bier wird gebraut. Hopfen wird hinzugefügt. Das Gesetz wird eingehalten) and the superlative (das älteste Gesetz, die meisten Brauereien, am liebsten). Read for the gist first, then find one number or one step per question.
help.tips[0].text: The passive says what is done, without saying who does it: Das Bier wird gebraut (the beer is brewed). Plural: Die Flaschen werden gefüllt. The participle is the Perfekt participle: brauen → gebraut, füllen → gefüllt, trinken → getrunken, hinzufügen → hinzugefügt. With a modal: Das Bier muss gekühlt werden. Who does it, if you want to say: von + dative: Das Bier wird von den Brauern gekocht. Use the passive for processes, recipes and rules.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: First the barley is put in water, then it is dried and ground.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: At the Oktoberfest seven million litres of beer are drunk.
help.tips[1].title: Superlative before a noun
help.tips[1].text: Before a noun the superlative takes an adjective ending: das älteste Gesetz, die größte Brauerei, die meisten Brauereien, der beliebteste Stil, das bekannteste Fest. Without a noun: am ältesten, am meisten, am liebsten. Irregular: gut → am besten, viel → am meisten, gern → am liebsten, groß → am größten, hoch → am höchsten.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The purity law is the oldest food law in the world still in force.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Germans like Pils best; most breweries are in Bavaria.
help.tips[1].check.q: Das Oktoberfest ist ____ Volksfest der Welt. (groß)
help.tips[1].check.why: Before a noun: das größte Volksfest (with ß and umlaut); am größten stands alone.
help.remember[0]: Passive: wird / werden + participle: Das Bier wird gebraut, die Flaschen werden gefüllt.
help.remember[1]: Superlative before a noun: das älteste Gesetz, die meisten Brauereien; alone: am liebsten, am meisten.
help.exam: Short factual texts about a product or a tradition, written with passive forms and comparisons, are a typical reading task at this level.
help.hook: Only water, barley and hops, by a law from 1516 that still applies: read how German beer is brewed and why the Oktoberfest began as a wedding.
help.vocab[1].example: Bier darf nur aus Wasser, Gerste und Hopfen gebraut werden.
passageTranslation:
On 23 April 1516 two Bavarian dukes made a law in Ingolstadt: beer may be brewed only from water, barley and hops. That is the Reinheitsgebot, the purity law, the oldest food law in the world still in force today. Yeast was not in the law, because it was not yet known. Today four ingredients are allowed: water, malt, hops and yeast.

How is beer brewed? First the barley is put in water, then dried. That turns barley into malt. The malt is ground and boiled with hot water. Then hops are added; they make the beer bitter. At the end yeast is added, and the beer must rest for some weeks. After that it is filled into barrels and bottles.

In Germany there are about 1,500 breweries and over 7,000 different beers. Most breweries are in Bavaria. Germans like Pils best. But they drink less and less: about 90 litres per person a year. Thirty years ago it was 140.

The best-known festival is the Oktoberfest in Munich. It began in 1810 as a wedding celebration: Prince Ludwig married Princess Therese, and the whole city was invited. Today about six million visitors come every year. They drink around seven million litres of beer, from glasses holding one litre. The glass is called a Maß, and a Maß costs over fifteen euros today.
